answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a vault as the anchor of the cost.
